cards.title: Use in-platform ROAS directionally, not across platforms
cards.claim: In-platform ROAS/CPA are helpful for directional feedback within a siloed platform, but comparing ROAS across platforms can mislead business-level budget decisions because attribution models, funnel position, and incremental impact differ.
cards.action: Use ROAS to compare campaigns within the same platform (e.g., two Meta campaigns). Avoid comparing a Google campaign ROAS to a Meta campaign ROAS or making larger business-level decisions based only on cross-platform ROAS.
applies_when: evaluating campaigns within a single platform
using in-platform metrics for directional campaign or ad feedback
do_not_use_when: making larger business-level budget decisions based only on in-platform ROAS
unknowns: How to adjust for different attribution models and funnel positions
What additional nuance or measurement system is required for cross-platform decisions
evidence_quotes: They are helpful in directional campaign feedback and ad feedback within the siloed platform.
what we do not want to do, what would be a big mistake is comparing a rorowaz number on a Google campaign to a rorowaz number on a meta campaign because they have different attribution models.

if we start comparing platforms, if we start zooming out and making larger business level decisions based on these numbers, that's where we can start to mislead ourselves and go into using low reliability, low data integrity level metric.

cards.title: Use new-customer revenue for finance-grade MER
cards.claim: Including returning customer revenue in MER makes it a terrible metric for indexing paid media performance over time because returning customer revenue has little to do with paid ads and may have returned anyway.
cards.action: Strip returning customer revenue out of MER; calculate a new-customer MER as new customer revenue divided by ad spend instead of total revenue divided by ad spend.
applies_when: indexing paid media performance over time
do_not_use_when: using total MER that includes returning customer revenue to judge paid media or acquisition performance
letting marketing take credit for returning customers that would have returned anyway
unknowns: What profitability threshold applies to new-customer MER in a given business

cards.title: Use geo holdout incrementality tests only with correct design
cards.claim: Incrementality testing can measure the impact of changing campaign types by holding out a geographic area and comparing revenue realization against control, but it is complicated and requires data science understanding.
cards.action: If running a geo incrementality test, split a country by states (or commuting zones in Australia if state selection is insufficient), hold out a control area, increase or cut spend in treatment, and measure revenue realization difference over a defined period such as 30 days; calculate incremental return on ad spend from the lift in new customer revenue against control.
applies_when: measuring incrementality of different campaign types
you have sufficient scale and at least a fundamental understanding of data science
you can isolate large control and treatment groups
do_not_use_when: using a simple spreadsheet to double budgets in states without correct test design
expecting statistically relevant results without proper setup
lacking data science understanding to approach this portion of the pyramid
